sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a bi-weekly podcast from the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学对话》，这是一档由美国心理学会为您带来的双周播播客。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Caitlin Luna.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人凯特琳·卢娜。

sentences.en: The topic for this episode is climate change.
sentences.zh: 本期节目的主题是气候变化。

sentences.en: And just a reminder before we get started, if you have any ideas for us, questions or comments, please email me at kluna at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前提醒大家，如果您有任何想法、问题或意见，请发电子邮件至 kluna@apa.org 联系我。

sentences.en: That's K-L-U-N-A at A-P-A dot org.
sentences.zh: 即 K-L-U-N-A ＠ A-P-A 点 org。

sentences.en: Polar vortexes, melting glaciers, historic flooding and devastating wildfires.
sentences.zh: 极地涡旋、冰川融化、历史性洪灾以及毁灭性的山火。

sentences.en: People are now ranking climate change as one of the world's top threats alongside ISIS and cyber attacks.
sentences.zh: 根据皮尤研究中心的一项最新民意调查显示，人们现在将气候变化列为世界首要威胁之一，与伊斯兰国和网络攻击并列。

sentences.en: That's according to a new Pew Research Center poll.
sentences.zh: 这是根据皮尤研究中心的一项最新民意调查得出的。

sentences.en: As we grapple with the warming world and increasingly unstable weather, our mental health is at risk.
sentences.zh: 当我们努力应对变暖的世界和日益不稳定的天气时，我们的心理健康正面临风险。

sentences.en: Many scientists predict that stress, anxiety, depression, and PTSD will increase as climate change's physical impacts accelerate.
sentences.zh: 许多科学家预测，随着气候变化带来的物理影响加速，压力、焦虑、抑郁和创伤后应激障碍将会增加。

sentences.en: Is there anything we can do to mitigate the mental health risks of climate change?
sentences.zh: 我们有什么办法可以缓解气候变化带来的心理健康风险吗？

sentences.en: Our guest is Dr. Susan Clayton, a professor of psychology and environmental studies at the College of Worcester.
sentences.zh: 我们的嘉宾是伍斯特学院心理学和环境研究教授苏珊·克莱顿博士。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Clayton.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，克莱顿博士。

sentences.en: Thank you, Caitlin.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，凯特琳。

sentences.en: I want to start off by talking about a book you co-edited called Psychology and Climate Change, Human Perceptions,
sentences.zh: 我想从讨论你共同主编的一本书开始，书名叫《心理学与气候变化：人类认知、

sentences.en: Impacts, and Responses.
sentences.zh: 影响与应对》。

sentences.en: How can psychology contribute to our understanding of climate change?
sentences.zh: 心理学如何促进我们对气候变化的理解？

sentences.en: I think that psychology is really important to climate change through both our set of research skills and tools as well as our focus on an individual level.
sentences.zh: 我认为心理学对气候非常重要，这既体现在我们的一套研究技能和工具上，也体现在我们对个体层面的关注上。

sentences.en: As psychologists, we really
sentences.zh: 作为心理学家，我们确实

sentences.en: conceptualize and prioritize individual well-being in a very broad way, more, I think, than any other discipline.
sentences.zh: 以非常广泛的方式概念化并优先考虑个体福祉，我认为这比任何其他学科都更甚。

sentences.en: And we also emphasize individual behavior and influences on individual behavior, which is very important to addressing climate change, both through policy preferences as well as
sentences.zh: 而且我们还强调个体行为以及对个体行为的影响，这对于应对气候变化非常重要，无论是通过政策偏好还是

sentences.en: through affecting individual behavioral choices.
sentences.zh: 通过影响个人的行为选择。

sentences.en: Do you think there's enough awareness about the mental health risks associated with climate change?
sentences.zh: 你认为人们对与气候变化相关的心理健康风险有足够的认识吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we often think of the physical elements, but what about mental health?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们经常想到物质要素，但心理健康呢？

sentences.en: No, I really think there hasn't been enough attention to this.
sentences.zh: 没有，我真的认为这方面没有得到足够的重视。

sentences.en: And you have this sort of trajectory with the discussion of climate change that first everybody thought about basically polar bears and on their little melting ice flows.
sentences.zh: 对于气候变化的讨论，你们经历了这样一个过程：起初每个人想到的基本都是北极熊和它们脚下正在融化的浮冰。

sentences.en: We have progressed a little bit to start thinking more about human impacts of climate change, but I don't think the impacts on mental health are
sentences.zh: 我们取得了一些进展，开始更多地思考气候变化对人类的影响，但我不认为心理健康受到的影响

sentences.en: something that very many people are aware of.
sentences.zh: 是很多人所意识到的。

sentences.en: And obviously, it's important for people to be aware because, as I mentioned in the intro, stress,
sentences.zh: 很显然，人们意识到这一点很重要，因为正如我在引言中提到的，压力、

sentences.en: anxiety, PTSD are all risks people face in addition to maybe like losing homes and devastating wildfires or flooding and things like that.
sentences.zh: 焦虑、创伤后应激障碍都是人们面临的风险，此外可能还有像失去家园、毁灭性的山火或洪水诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So do you think we're at a point now where awareness is increasing or by doing interviews like this, it will increase or do it, you know, as you write your
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为我们现在已经到了这样一个节点：人们的意识正在增强，或者通过做这样的采访它会增强，或者你知道的，正如你写

sentences.en: books, as you do your studies?
sentences.zh: 书、做研究时那样？

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Certainly, there seems to be, you know, more media attention.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道的，媒体的关注度似乎确实更高了。

sentences.en: And I certainly hope that there's increasing attention and partly because we are getting more and more evidence.
sentences.zh: 我当然希望关注度能不断增加，部分原因是我们正在获得越来越多的证据。

sentences.en: So we don't have to just speculate.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不必只是猜测。

sentences.en: We can start to look at what the research is showing.
sentences.zh: 我们可以开始看看研究显示了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And for people who've already been affected by a climate related natural disaster, like wildfires we saw in California in the fall, or coastal flooding, what are some of
sentences.zh: 对于那些已经受到气候相关自然灾害影响的人来说，比如我们在秋季看到的加州山火，或者海岸洪水，经历过此类事件后人们会产生哪些

sentences.en: the psychological symptoms people experience after an event like that?
sentences.zh: 心理症状？

sentences.en: There's definitely impacts on your mental health.
sentences.zh: 这绝对会对你的心理健康产生影响。

sentences.en: You know, even though we've only recently started thinking about climate change impacts, there have been natural disasters forever, and they've been studied for some time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，尽管我们最近才开始关注气候变化的影响，但自然灾害一直存在，并且已经被研究了一段时间。

sentences.en: So we know that they tend to lead to an increase in things like post-traumatic stress disorder, depression, and things you might not be as aware of, like substance abuse.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，它们往往会导致创伤后应激障碍、抑郁症等问题的增加，以及你可能不那么了解的事情，比如药物滥用。

sentences.en: And what about something maybe less, a little less acute, but still nonetheless important, maybe feelings of hopelessness, feelings of loss?
sentences.zh: 那么那些可能不那么严重、但同样重要的事情呢，比如无助感、失落感？

sentences.en: Do those increase in the wake of a natural disaster as people try to recover?
sentences.zh: 在自然灾害发生后，随着人们试图恢复，这些感觉会增加吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: People often use the term grief to describe the responses of people who have experienced it.
sentences.zh: 人们经常用“悲伤”这个词来描述经历过这些的人的反应。

sentences.en: There's a sadness associated with what is lost, which may be your home, which of
sentences.zh: 与失去的东西相关的一种悲伤，这可能是你的家，当然它在心理上极其重要，还有你的社区，你知道的，对你的经济状况有非常实际的影响。

sentences.en: course is extremely psychologically important, your community, your, you know, very practical impacts on your economic well-being.
sentences.zh: 当然，这在心理上极其重要，还有你的社区，你知道的，对你的经济状况有非常实际的影响。

sentences.en: And another impact of these kinds of natural disasters is often an increase on social tensions.
sentences.zh: 这类自然灾害的另一个影响通常是社会紧张局势的加剧。

sentences.en: So research has shown increases in things like domestic violence, too.
sentences.zh: 因此研究表明，家庭暴力等现象也有所增加。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it can really have a ripple effect beyond the initial loss of dealing with loss of a home or, you know, injuries, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实会产生连锁反应，除了最初应对失去家园或受伤等损失之外，还有诸如此类的情况。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so you've been involved in a lot of APA's work about the application of psychology to climate change.
sentences.zh: 因此，你一直参与美国心理学会关于将心理学应用于气候变化的很多工作。

sentences.en: We had a task force on the interface between psychology and global climate change that published a report almost 10 years ago, back in 2009.
sentences.zh: 我们曾有一个关于心理学与全球气候变化接口的工作组，在将近10年前的2009年发布了一份报告。

sentences.en: And also APA's reports in collaboration with EcoAmerica that were published in 2014 and 17.
sentences.zh: 还有美国心理学会与EcoAmerica合作于2014年和2017年发布的报告。

sentences.en: So you've been involved in this space for quite a while and also with your work at the college.
sentences.zh: 所以你在这个领域已经有一段时间了，并且你在大学里也开展了相关工作。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about what got you interested in environmental studies and psychology?
sentences.zh: 你能聊聊是什么让你对环境研究和心理学产生兴趣的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, sure.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: Well, it's a long story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，说来话长。

sentences.en: I'll try to sort of summarize.
sentences.zh: 我尽量总结一下吧。

sentences.en: I'm trained as a social psychologist, and I've always been interested in people's reactions to social issues, you know, group identity, those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 我的专业背景是社会心理学家，我一直对人们对社会问题的反应很感兴趣，你知道的，群体认同，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And I also care about the environment.
sentences.zh: 而且我也很关心环境。

sentences.en: And I started to notice just through my informal observations and my readings that, you know, the natural environment was a really important source of experience for people.
sentences.zh: 我开始通过非正式的观察和阅读注意到，自然环境确实是人们体验的一个重要来源。

sentences.en: And it was one that had both meaning to them as individuals and also had sort of social significance.
sentences.zh: 它既对作为个体的他们有意义，也具有某种社会意义。

sentences.en: And a lot of parents, for example, are very deliberate about introducing their children to the natural world and telling them how we need to take care of the natural world.
sentences.zh: 例如，许多父母非常刻意地引导他们的孩子接触自然世界，并告诉他们我们需要如何爱护自然世界。

sentences.en: So I just started to think of the natural environment as a source of psychological influence.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始把自然环境看作一种心理影响的来源。

sentences.en: And then as attention to climate change got, you know, increased, I started to think about the impacts of climate change on that sort of psychological as well as social well-being.
sentences.zh: 然后，随着对气候变化的关注度不断提高，我开始思考气候变化对这种心理以及社会福祉的影响。

sentences.en: And what about just even if you're not experiencing something directly like a climate-related natural
sentences.zh: 那么，即使你没有直接经历某些事情，比如气候相关的自然

sentences.en: disaster, but just watching that constant stream of news coverage about polar ice melting and extreme weather, what does that do to our mental health collectively?
sentences.zh: 灾害，而只是看着关于北极冰层融化和极端天气的源源不断的新闻报道，这对我们集体的心理健康有什么影响？

sentences.en: And for people who are kind of more bystanders in that regard?
sentences.zh: 对于在这方面更像是旁观者的人来说呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's a great question, because we usually think about the people who are directly influenced by something and what they might be suffering.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个很好的问题，因为我们通常只考虑那些直接受到某种影响的人以及他们可能遭受的痛苦。

sentences.en: But when it comes to climate change, even people who aren't experiencing the direct impacts are nevertheless facing this big deal thing
sentences.zh: 但说到气候变化，即使是没有经历直接影响的人，也同样面临着这个重大问题

sentences.en: that some might, you know, call an existential challenge.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会称之为生存挑战。

sentences.en: So even though you might not have been individually affected, you might be experiencing certainly an increase in stress, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使你可能没有受到个体层面的影响，你肯定也会经历压力的增加等情况。

sentences.en: And the APA has their Stress in America survey.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学会有一项“美国压力”调查。

sentences.en: And the most recent version found, I think, about 50% of people said that climate change was a significant source of stress for them.
sentences.zh: 最新的调查结果显示，我想大约有50%的人表示气候变化是他们压力的一个重要来源。

sentences.en: And of course, we have a lot of stress in our lives.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们的生活中有很多压力。

sentences.en: But for some people, that one additional source of stress might kind of push them to a point where they feel that they can't cope very well.
sentences.zh: 但对某些人来说，这一个额外的压力源可能会把他们推向一个感到自己无法很好应对的境地。

sentences.en: So yeah, how do you I mean, this feels very far away at some point, some of these things we're
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你怎么看——我的意思是，在某些时候，当我们看到极地以及我们在这一前沿看到的一些重大变化时，其中一些事情感觉非常遥远，我能想象这很容易让人感到无助。

sentences.en: seeing on as we look at look to, you know, the Arctic, and some of these big changes we're seeing on that front, it's easy, I'm imagining to feel helpless.
sentences.zh: 当我看到极地以及我们在这一前沿看到的一些重大变化时，其中一些事情感觉非常遥远，我能想象这很容易让人感到无助。

sentences.en: I felt that way, too.
sentences.zh: 我也曾有过这种感觉。

sentences.en: And you see all that's going on, and you wonder what you can do as an individual.
sentences.zh: 当你看到正在发生的一切时，你会想作为个人你能做些什么。

sentences.en: So how do you stay aware of what's happening without getting overwhelmed by, by what you're seeing?
sentences.zh: 那么，如何在不被你所看到的东西压垮的情况下，保持对正在发生的事情的关注呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think a really important problem for people is how to stay optimistic.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为人们面临的一个真正重要的问题是如何保持乐观。

sentences.en: And certainly, optimism is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 当然，乐观是一件好事。

sentences.en: And optimism is associated with, you know, being more resilient to negative events.
sentences.zh: 乐观与对负面事件具有更强的韧性息息相关。

sentences.en: I would say two factors are really important.
sentences.zh: 我认为有两个因素非常重要。

sentences.en: One is to to stay informed and and think of things that you can do.
sentences.zh: 一个是保持知情，并思考你能做的事情。

sentences.en: Because not only will you be maybe addressing the problem, you'll also feel more empowered, and you'll have a higher sense of efficacy.
sentences.zh: 因为你不仅可能在解决问题，还会感到更有力量，并且会有更高的效能感。

sentences.en: And I think that that feeling of helplessness is a real problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种无助感是一个真正的问题。

sentences.en: So when people do identify something they can do, that helps avoid that problem.
sentences.zh: 因此，当人们确实确定了某件他们可以做的事情时，这有助于避免这个问题。

sentences.en: And the second thing would be to to form groups to form communities with other people.
sentences.zh: 第二件事是组建群体，与其他人建立社群。

sentences.en: Because social bonds are so incredibly important to our mental health.
sentences.zh: 因为社会纽带对我们的心理健康极其重要。

sentences.en: And also forming these groups make us feel more powerful.
sentences.zh: 而且组建这些群体也让我们感到更有力量。

sentences.en: Because of course, groups can get things accomplished that individuals can't.
sentences.zh: 因为毫无疑问，群体能办成个人办不到的事情。

sentences.en: And feel more hopeful.
sentences.zh: 并且感到更有希望。

sentences.en: And just share information with each other so we can actually be more effective.
sentences.zh: 互相分享信息，这样我们实际上就能更有效率。

sentences.en: And I think people can can form groups in a variety of different ways, depending on how they want to respond to this issue.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们可以通过各种不同的方式组建群体，这取决于他们希望如何应对这个问题。

sentences.en: They can just form communities to kind of inform themselves about the likely impacts of climate change, or to talk about their emotional response.
sentences.zh: 他们可以仅仅建立社群来让自己了解气候变化的可能影响，或者谈论他们的情绪反应。

sentences.en: Or they can form communities that become, you know, politically active and try to work within the local community or a national level to address issues of climate change.
sentences.zh: 或者他们可以建立变得具有政治活跃度的社群，并尝试在当地社区或国家层面努力解决气候变化问题。

sentences.en: And again, hopefully that will have an impact.
sentences.zh: 同样，希望这会产生影响。

sentences.en: But from the individual's perspective, it will almost certainly enhance their mental health.
sentences.zh: 但从个人的角度来看，它几乎肯定会增进他们的心理健康。

sentences.en: And what about it is individuals?
sentences.zh: 那么作为个人呢？

sentences.en: I mean, talking about being a collective and making change.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谈到作为一个集体并做出改变。

sentences.en: But as an individual, is it something as simple, things you can do to help with climate change is to
sentences.zh: 但作为个人，这是否就像你可以做一些简单的事情来帮助应对气候变化一样

sentences.en: make small behavioral changes like, you know, using less plastic silverware or consuming less meat?
sentences.zh: 做出小的行为改变，比如少用塑料餐具或少吃肉？

sentences.en: I mean, what are some of those tangible things people can do in their individual lives?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们在个人生活中可以做哪些切实可行的事情？

sentences.en: And do they have a big impact?
sentences.zh: 它们会产生重大影响吗？

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 会的。

sentences.en: I know that people can think, oh, nothing, any, nothing I can do as an individual will make any difference.
sentences.zh: 我知道人们可能会想，噢，没有什么，任何作为个人我能做的事都不会带来任何改变。

sentences.en: But, but actually, I think, you know, at some level, only individuals can make a difference through their collective choices.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我认为，在某种程度上，只有个人才能通过他们的集体选择带来改变。

sentences.en: And if enough individuals make choices, it can have a big impact.
sentences.zh: 如果足够多的个人做出选择，就会产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: It's not all just about what organizations and industry does.
sentences.zh: 这并不完全取决于组织和工业所做的事情。

sentences.en: So one of the most important things you can do as an individual is to try and affect public policy by, by voting, by, by calling
sentences.zh: 因此，作为个人你能做的最重要的事情之一，就是通过投票、通过致电

sentences.en: your government representatives and letting them know that you support pro-environmental policy.
sentences.zh: 政府代表并让他们知道你支持亲环境的政策，来试图影响公共政策。

sentences.en: And the same thing is true for affecting industry.
sentences.zh: 影响工业也是同样的道理。

sentences.en: You can have an impact on companies through your consumer choices.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过消费选择对公司产生影响。

sentences.en: And you can also contact them.
sentences.zh: 你也可以联系他们。

sentences.en: And, and industries are responding to these, you know, to consumer attitudes.
sentences.zh: 而且，工业界正在对这些，你知道的，对消费者的态度做出回应。

sentences.en: So you can really make a difference there.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的可以在那里发挥作用。

sentences.en: But of course, we also want to do things that feel more concrete at a behavioral level.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们也想做一些在行为层面上感觉更具体的事情。

sentences.en: Some of the most important things are to find ways to reduce your use of fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 其中一些最重要的事情是找到减少化石燃料使用的方法。

sentences.zh: 所以你可以处于某种，呃，社会脆弱状态。

sentences.zh: 当然，你也可以处于地理脆弱状态。

sentences.zh: 所以位于，呃，沿海地区或地势低洼的岛屿的人们，是非常脆弱的。

sentences.en: Um, you can be financially vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可能会在财务上很脆弱。

sentences.en: People who have more financial resources are usually better able to protect themselves, um, than those who have fewer.
sentences.zh: 拥有更多财务资源的人通常比资源较少的人更有能力保护自己。

sentences.en: But I, I want to highlight in particular the fact that children are more vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 但我，我想特别强调这样一个事实，即儿童更脆弱。

sentences.en: Um, and of course they're more vulnerable because they're going to be living with the consequences of what we do now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然他们更脆弱，因为他们将带着我们现在所做之事的后果生活下去。

sentences.en: Uh, uh, so they're going to just experience climate change to a greater extent, but also the kinds of, uh, effects and, uh, events they experience when
sentences.zh: 呃，呃，所以他们将更大程度地经历气候变化，而且他们在年轻时

sentences.en: they're young can have a disproportionate impact.
sentences.zh: 经历的各种，呃，影响和，呃，事件可能会产生不成比例的影响。

sentences.en: Um, you know, new research by, or, or fairly new research by psychologists is looking at the, the way that, um, experiencing stress and trauma as a

sentences.en: child may have permanent impacts on your, uh, sort of cognitive processes and emotional, um,

sentences.en: self-regulation, for example, as an adult, um, uh, high levels of pollution, which can be associated
sentences.zh: 自我调节产生永久性的影响，呃，高水平的污染，这可能与

sentences.en: with, uh, with the climate because we have, you know, higher temperatures lead to higher levels of
sentences.zh: 关于气候问题，你知道的，因为气温升高会导致

sentences.en: ground level ozone, higher levels of pollution have effects on our cognitive processes that may again, have permanent effects into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 地面臭氧增加，污染加剧会对我们的认知过程产生影响，并且可能在成年后留下永久性的影响。

sentences.en: And of course, um, children can be physiologically damaged more easily as, uh, at a young age because their, their bodily systems aren't all fully developed.
sentences.zh: 当然，由于孩子们在年幼时身体系统尚未完全发育，他们的生理机能更容易受到损害。

sentences.en: Um, for example, they are not as good at regulating their own temperatures.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们调节自身体温的能力较差。

sentences.en: So they might respond more strongly to, to high levels of heat and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对高温等环境的反应可能会更强烈。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, uh, talking about children, um, obviously the earth's growing population contributes to environmental probleMs. That's something that's noted and talked about frequently.
sentences.zh: 而且，说到孩子，地球不断增长的人口显然加剧了环境问题，这一点大家有目共睹，也经常被讨论。

sentences.en: And some people are deciding not to have children due to climate change, or perhaps maybe only having one child, maybe adopting that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 有些人因为气候变化决定不要孩子，或者可能只生一个孩子，也许会选择领养之类的。

sentences.en: Um, what are your thoughts on this?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting because people are very, it's, it's like the third rail topic.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为人们对这个话题非常敏感，就像碰触高压电线一样。

sentences.en: People get very, uh, defensive about talking about the choice to have children.
sentences.zh: 在谈到生育选择时，人们往往会表现得非常防备。

sentences.en: Uh, I just recently, as part of a class exercise had my students distribute a questionnaire that asked people about environmental attitudes and
sentences.zh: 我最近在一次课堂练习中，让学生们分发了一份问卷，询问人们对环境的态度以及

sentences.en: whether they thought families should be encouraged to have no more than two children.
sentences.zh: 他们是否认为应该鼓励家庭最多只生两个孩子。

sentences.en: And my students reported that, of course, everybody had positive environmental attitudes, but they were very reluctant to say there should be limits on, on family size.
sentences.zh: 我的学生反馈说，当然每个人都有积极的环境保护态度，但他们非常不情愿承认应该对家庭规模进行限制。

sentences.en: Um, I think we do need to acknowledge that, uh, you know, more people means more stress on environmental resources.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们确实需要承认，更多的人口意味着对环境资源的更大压力。

sentences.en: It's just, uh, you know, it's basic physics now.
sentences.zh: 这就像是基本的物理学原理一样。

sentences.en: So I think that we, let me back up a second.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，让我稍微退一步说。

sentences.en: I, you know, there are all kinds of reasons not to, uh, have laws about the number of children people have, but
sentences.zh: 你知道的，反对制定人口生育法律的理由有很多，但

sentences.en: I think what would be a better approach would be to provide more options that allow people to have the number of children they want and not more than they want.
sentences.zh: 我认为更好的方法是提供更多选择，让人们能够生想要数量的孩子，而不会超过他们的预期。

sentences.en: So more federal access to, um, uh, you know, contraception and also sex education, I think that would go a long way to, um, keeping our population in check.
sentences.zh: 因此，增加联邦对避孕措施以及性教育的普及，我认为这对于控制人口规模大有帮助。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Do you think that will increase as, as time goes on?
sentences.zh: 你认为随着时间的推移，这种情况会增加吗？

sentences.en: And as, like you said, children are more vulnerable to the effects of climate change.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，儿童更容易受到气候变化的影响。

sentences.en: And as we see what is set in motion to happen to the planet, do you think that this could become more of an issue that's talked about in, in the media?
sentences.zh: 随着我们看到地球正在发生的种种变化，你认为这会成为媒体上更多讨论的议题吗？

sentences.en: You mean population control?
sentences.zh: 你是说人口控制？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Population control.
sentences.zh: 人口控制。

sentences.en: I, I would imagine so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I mean, even if you don't think that there are too many people now, you know, when there are whatever 7.3 billion, when it gets to 10 billion, you might then think,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使你现在不觉得人口过剩，当人口达到73亿，或者未来达到100亿时，你可能就会觉得

sentences.en: oh, now there are too many.
sentences.zh: 哦，现在人太多了。

sentences.en: So I, I do believe at some point it's going to become more of a topic of discussion than it is now.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信，在某个时候，这会比现在成为更受关注的讨论话题。

sentences.en: And one thing when I was researching this topic, I found really interesting and frightening at the same time was basically how the effects of climate change,
sentences.zh: 我在研究这个课题时发现了一件既非常有趣又令人恐慌的事情，那就是气候变化的影响

sentences.en: even if we were to stop all, stop in our tracks, no more emissions, you know, no more population growth, everyone becomes a vegetarian and, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 即使我们立刻停下所有脚步，不再有碳排放，没有人口增长，每个人都变成素食主义者，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Even if we were to do all that right now, there would, the effects would still continue in some ways because they've been set in motion
sentences.zh: 即使我们现在就做到这一切，其影响在某些方面仍会继续，因为这些影响已经由于

sentences.en: from the paSt. Um, so in your, in your understanding as a psychologist and environmental, um, scholar,
sentences.zh: 过去的累积而被触发了。那么，以你作为心理学家和环境学者的理解，

sentences.en: that's pretty, it's pretty frightening, I guess, to, to know that this, all these changes could still happen, but we were, we would be mitigating future changes.
sentences.zh: 了解到所有这些变化仍会发生，但我们只是在减轻未来的变化，我想这挺让人害怕的。

sentences.en: But so what are your, what are your thoughts on that?
sentences.zh: 那么，对此你有什么看法？

sentences.en: I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: And that definitely leads to, contributes to the sense of helplessness, uh, that people feel because you feel like, oh, it's already, they're already going to be,
sentences.zh: 这无疑会导致并加剧人们感到的无助感，因为你会觉得，哦，这一切

sentences.en: the climate is already changing and there's already going to be more changes.
sentences.zh: 气候已经在变化了，而且还会有更多的变化发生。

sentences.en: So I can't do anything.
sentences.zh: 所以我什么也做不了。

sentences.en: I think we need to emphasize more strongly the difference between, you know, one amount of change and another amount of change.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要更强有力地强调一种变化程度与另一种变化程度之间的区别。

sentences.en: Um, the, uh, intergovernmental panel on climate change released a report in October that, uh, delineated the difference between what if the
sentences.zh: 联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会在十月发布了一份报告，阐明了

sentences.en: temperature goes up by 1.5 degrees Celsius versus two degrees Celsius and identified a really big gap in impacts of 1.5 versus two degrees.
sentences.zh: 气温上升1.5摄氏度与上升2摄氏度之间的区别，并指出了1.5度与2度在影响上的巨大差距。

sentences.en: So even though I think we have to acknowledge the climate has already changed, is already changing and will continue to change, there's still a lot of difference
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管我认为我们必须承认气候已经改变、正在改变并将继续改变，但我们在

sentences.en: we can make in terms of the, um, the amount of that change and a difference that is going to make a difference in how we experience it.
sentences.zh: 这种变化的程度以及它对我们切身体验所产生的影响方面，仍然可以做出很大改变。

sentences.en: Mm hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So there's still time to make changes.
sentences.zh: 所以现在做出改变还为时不晚。

sentences.en: You know, it's not, even though we can't prevent everything that's been set in motion, there's still a lot of opportunities to mitigate the effects.
sentences.zh: 要知道，尽管我们无法阻止所有已经启动的进程，但仍有许多机会来减轻这些影响。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I, you know, I mentioned the intergovernmental panel on climate change, um, which I'm sure some people are familiar with, uh, you know, an international body of people that
sentences.zh: 而且我提到了政府间气候变化专门委员会，相信有些人对此很熟悉，这是一个国际组织，

sentences.en: have produced reports on the, the evidence for and impacts of climate change.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在产出关于气候变化证据及其影响的报告。

sentences.en: And I'm, um, an author on the next report to the report, they produce reports periodically, and I'll be participating in the next one.
sentences.zh: 我是下一份报告的作者之一，他们定期发布报告，我也将参与下一份报告的工作。

sentences.en: Um, it's a, it's a huge and very serious body and they wouldn't be doing this if they thought there was, it couldn't make any difference.
sentences.zh: 这是一个庞大且极其严肃的机构，如果他们认为无济于事，是不会做这件事的。

sentences.en: They're really doing this to provide the information that can guide public policy and choices that will affect, um, the kinds of future we face.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做实际上是为了提供能够指导公共政策和选择的信息，从而影响我们未来面临的局面。

sentences.en: Mm hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I want to touch on, uh, people who are climate change deniers.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈那些气候变化否认者。

sentences.en: Can you talk about the psychology of denial?
sentences.zh: 你能聊聊否认心理学吗？

sentences.en: I'm sure that's a very fascinating topic to get into.
sentences.zh: 我确信这是一个非常引人入胜的切入点。

sentences.en: It is kind of fascinating.
sentences.zh: 确实挺引人入胜的。

sentences.en: And the sad thing is that there are many, many reasons, um, to be a denier of climate change.
sentences.zh: 可悲的是，人们选择否认气候变化有着种种原因。

sentences.en: And to be honest, at some level, we're all deniers because if we really thought that it was as big an issue as it is, if we really took that to heart, um,
sentences.zh: 老实说，在某种程度上，我们所有人都是否认者，因为如果我们真的认为这是一个如此严重的问题，如果我们真的把它放在心上，

sentences.en: we would be acting differently.
sentences.zh: 我们的行为就会有所不同。

sentences.en: And I, I include myself in that group.
sentences.zh: 我也把我自己归入这一类人。

sentences.en: Uh, you know, I, I certainly use, um, a lot of, I produce a lot of carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我肯定也在使用很多能源，产生了大量的碳排放。

sentences.en: It's a very hard thing for us to come to terms because at some level, it's hard for us to believe that we as a species can affect the
sentences.zh: 我们要接受这一点非常困难，因为在某种程度上，我们很难相信作为物种的我们能够影响

sentences.en: environment, you know, the whole global environment.
sentences.zh: 环境，你知道，整个全球环境。

sentences.en: Um, it's hard to believe that there are some groups for whom that's really hard to believe.
sentences.zh: 很难相信，对某些群体来说，这一点真的很难相信。

sentences.en: For example, uh, some colleagues of mine, uh, from anthropology and, uh, biology studied the Amish, um, community and the Amish can't really
sentences.zh: 例如，我的一些来自人类学和生物学的同事研究了阿米什人社区，阿米什人很难

sentences.en: accept climate change because they just don't think humans can, you know, God is in charge of the world.
sentences.zh: 接受气候变化，因为他们认为人类做不到这一点，上帝才主宰世界。

sentences.en: Humans can't affect the world.
sentences.zh: 人类无法影响世界。

sentences.en: And there are other religious communities that might also feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 还有其他一些宗教社群可能也有同样的感受。

sentences.en: So we have these sort of ideological beliefs that make it difficult for us to acknowledge this is happening.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有这种意识形态信仰，让我们很难承认这一切正在发生。

sentences.en: And we want to justify the system we live in as opposed to say, well, this is not working.
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于为我们赖以生存的体制辩护，而不是去说，这套体制行不通了。

sentences.en: We need to start over.
sentences.zh: 我们需要重新开始。

sentences.en: That's very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这非常困难。

sentences.en: Of course, we also, to the extent that climate change is scary and it is scary.
sentences.zh: 当然，鉴于气候变化是可怕的，而且它确实很可怕。

sentences.en: Um, you know, we're trying to protect ourselves by denying it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们试图通过否认它来保护自己。

sentences.en: So to maintain positive emotions.
sentences.zh: 从而维持积极的情绪。

sentences.en: And then of course, it has to be acknowledged that, um, in the United States in particular, as well as some other countries, uh, climate change has become really politicized.
sentences.zh: 当然，必须承认的是，特别是在美国以及其他一些国家，气候变化已经变得高度政治化。

sentences.en: So it can be a marker of group identity to say you do or do not believe in climate change regardless of what you might truly think.
sentences.zh: 因此，无论你内心真正怎么想，声称自己相信或不相信气候变化都可以成为群体认同的标志。

sentences.en: So that I think that that political identity gets in the way of people just addressing the issue as an issue.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种政治身份认同阻碍了人们单纯把这个问题当作一个问题来处理。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, when people deny climate change, do you think they're sort of just, do you think it's, it is more motivated by politics
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当人们否认气候变化时，你觉得这更多是出于政治动机，

sentences.en: or you said like, just people are just don't believe that I'm not seeing this in front of my face.
sentences.zh: 还是如你所说，人们只是不相信，因为我没有亲眼看到它发生？

sentences.zh: 你知道的，我没有看到湖泊每年冬天都结冰，或者像这种极地涡旋。

sentences.en: That was a common thing that came up.
sentences.zh: 这是一个经常被提及的现象。

sentences.en: Um, you know, this, these deep freeze, like, okay, how can the world be warming if it's, if we're having these extreme cold temperatures?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这种严寒天气让人觉得，好吧，如果我们正经历极端低温，世界怎么可能在变暖呢？

sentences.en: Um, that's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, and we, of course, you know, it's easy for us to try and, uh, understand something in concrete terms and this very abstract issue of climate change.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们很容易用具体的概念去理解事物，而气候变化却是一个非常抽象的问题。

sentences.zh: 所以现在我窗外正在下雪。

sentences.en: Um, those are really hard for us to, to kind of grasp and take seriously.
sentences.zh: 这些确实很难让我们切实去理解并认真对待。

sentences.zh: 我也非常希望如此。

sentences.en: Um, but my first response would be,
sentences.zh: 但我的第一反应是，

sentences.zh: 我不确定这是否应该是我们的策略。

sentences.en: And one reason I say that is that, you know, people resist having their mind changed.
sentences.zh: 我这么说的一个原因是，你知道的，人们抗拒改变自己的想法。

sentences.en: So it sounds like you're giving in, you know, you're losing in the persuasion battle at some level.
sentences.zh: 所以这听起来就像你在妥协，在某种程度上你在说服之战中输了。

sentences.en: So when you say to somebody either explicitly or even implicitly, I'm going to bring you over to my way of thinking you're requiring them to give ground at some level.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你明示或暗示地对某人说“我要把你拉到我的思维方式这边来”时，你是在要求他们在某种程度上做出让步。

sentences.en: So I would say, um, instead of kind of focusing on, Oh, you have to accept climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，与其纠结于“哦，你必须接受气候变化”，

sentences.en: Let's focus on the actions.
sentences.zh: 不如把重点放在行动上。

sentences.en: Um, what is it that we want people to do?
sentences.zh: 我们到底想让人们做什么？

sentences.en: Do we want them to support higher, uh, you know, fuel efficiency standards?
sentences.zh: 我们是希望他们支持更高的燃油效率标准吗？

sentences.en: Let's focus on some of the reasons for doing that and not require them to accept climate change firSt. Um, there are lots of, uh, what have been
sentences.zh: 让我们专注于做这件事的一些理由，而不是要求他们首先接受气候变化。嗯，有很多所谓的

sentences.en: called co-benefits to addressing climate change.
sentences.zh: 应对气候变化的“协同效益”。

sentences.en: So sort of basically side effects that will have positive impacts on people.
sentences.zh: 也就是基本上会对人们产生积极影响的副作用。

sentences.en: Um, and a lot of those might have to do with energy efficiency and saving money.
sentences.zh: 其中许多可能与提高能效和节省开支有关。

sentences.en: Um, a lot of them have to, a lot of them have to do with health as, you know, as a species, um,
sentences.zh: 它们中有很多与健康有关，作为人类物种，

sentences.en: there would be a lot of benefits for us in, you know, driving less and eating less
sentences.zh: 如果我们少开车、少吃红肉、多走路，

sentences.en: red meat and walking more and, uh, um, you know, reducing our air pollution so that we weren't exposed to such, uh, air quality that leads to respiratory disorders.
sentences.zh: 并减少空气污染，从而避免接触导致呼吸系统疾病的空气质量，这对我们会有很多好处。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of positive reasons to get people to engage in these, uh, climate protective behaviors.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多积极的理由促使人们参与这些保护气候的行为。

sentences.en: But motivating change is obviously always difficult.
sentences.zh: 但激发行为改变显然一直都很困难。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, and, and, and I didn't want to totally ignore your question about changing the minds of climate change deniers.
sentences.zh: 而且我并不想完全忽略你关于改变气候变化否认者想法的问题。

sentences.en: So there are some ways to make the message more effective.
sentences.zh: 所以有一些方法可以让信息传递得更有效。

sentences.en: And, um, a couple of things that might specifically relate to their motives for denial are, uh, to make sure that
sentences.zh: 其中有几点可能与他们否认的动机直接相关，那就是确保

sentences.en: they're the messenger, the person who's delivering the climate change message is somebody they truSt.
sentences.zh: 传递气候变化信息的人是他们信任的人。

sentences.en: You know, so, um, somebody who might be seen as a member of their own group, as opposed to an outsider who's trying to, again, to force their own, uh, position on them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一个被视为他们自己群体成员的人，而不是那种试图把自己的立场强加给他们的局外人。

sentences.en: And another is that you can tie it to values that they endorse.
sentences.zh: 另一个方法是将其与他们认同的价值观联系起来。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's psychological research looking at how conservatives and liberals on average tend to endorse slightly different sets of values.
sentences.zh: 心理学研究表明，保守派和自由派平均而言倾向于认同略有不同的价值观。

sentences.en: So if you're talking to a more conservative group, you might emphasize the values that, uh, are more
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在和一个更保守的群体交谈，你可能会强调那些对他们更重要的价值观；

sentences.en: important to them and to a liberal group, you emphasize those different sets of values.
sentences.zh: 而对于自由派群体，你则强调另一套不同的价值观。

sentences.en: And I think you can come up with climate change messages that are really targeted towards a particular audience.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以提出真正针对特定受众的气候变化信息。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about your, um, your other research was focuses on understanding and promoting a healthy relationships between humans and nature.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈你的另一项研究，该研究侧重于理解和促进人与自然之间的健康关系。

sentences.en: And so you've done a lot of research at zoos.
sentences.zh: 你已经在动物园做了很多研究。

sentences.en: How do zoos help people feel more connected to nature?
sentences.zh: 动物园是如何帮助人们感觉与自然更加亲近的？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I, this is something that I just fell across and I hadn't, it didn't occur to me until I happened to be talking to some people who worked at zoos.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这是我偶然涉足的一个领域，在与一些在动物园工作的人交谈之前，我从未想过这一点。

sentences.en: So like everybody else, I went to a zoo as a child and then I took my children to the zoo, but I didn't think of it, uh, much other than that.
sentences.zh: 就像其他人一样，我小时候去过动物园，后来也带自己的孩子去动物园，但我没有作过更多的思考。

sentences.en: But talking to these zoo researchers, I realized that for many people, the zoo is a place to encounter the natural world.
sentences.zh: 但通过与这些动物园研究人员交谈，我意识到对许多人来说，动物园是接触自然世界的一个场所。

sentences.en: Um, and it's one of the few places where they can do that.
sentences.zh: 而且这是他们能够做到这一点的极少数几个地方之一。

sentences.en: And zoos really attract a very broad, you know, range of people.
sentences.zh: 动物园确实吸引了非常广泛的人群。

sentences.en: Um, many zoos will have, you know, free days so that, uh, money is not a barrier.
sentences.zh: 许多动物园会设立免费开放日，这样金钱就不会成为障碍。

sentences.en: Um, many, many children will go in school groups.
sentences.zh: 许多孩子会以学校团体身份前往。

sentences.en: So a lot of people go to the zoo.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多人会去动物园。

sentences.en: Um, and Bob Cialdini once said, you know, if you're a social psychologist, you should go where the people are.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·查尔迪尼曾说过，如果你是一名社会心理学家，你应该去人多的地方。

sentences.en: So I thought, well, I'll go where the people are.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，好吧，那我就去人多的地方。

sentences.en: Um, and then their, their social situations.
sentences.zh: 而且那里存在社交场景。

sentences.en: So people are not just individuals going and looking animals.
sentences.zh: 人们不是仅仅作为个体去观看动物。

sentences.en: They're people going in groups to look at animals and then sort of react to those animals in groups and give each other messages about how do I feel about this animal?
sentences.zh: 他们是结伴去观看动物，然后以群体形式对这些动物做出反应，并互相交流“我对这只动物有什么感觉”的信息，

sentences.en: And, uh, you know, what, what is, what is our relationship with these animals?
sentences.zh: 以及我们与这些动物的关系是什么。

sentences.en: And then, you know, finally zoos have a mission.
sentences.zh: 最后，动物园是有其使命的。

sentences.en: They do think of themselves as conservation organizations.
sentences.zh: 它们确实认为自己是自然保护组织。

sentences.en: So they are trying to deliver messages to people that encourage them to, uh, kind of feel a more supportive relationship with the natural world.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们试图向人们传递信息，鼓励人们对自然世界产生一种更具支持性的关系。

sentences.en: And overall, did you feel like people's, um, who you interviewed and you studied, do you feel like that did increase their connection to nature by being at a zoo?
sentences.zh: 总体而言，你觉得你采访和研究过的人，在动物园的经历确实增进了他们与自然的联系吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Some of the, some of the research definitely has suggested that.
sentences.zh: 其中一些、一些研究确实表明了这一点。

sentences.en: Um, and I often, you know, there are people who are critical of zoos and, um, you know, for some legitimate reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我经常，你知道的，有些人对动物园持批评态度，嗯，你知道的，有一些合理的理由。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 而

sentences.en: my response is always, I don't have to have a philosophical position on zoos.
sentences.zh: 我的回答一直是，我对动物园不需要有什么哲学立场。

sentences.en: I'm just studying the reality of zoos.
sentences.zh: 我只是在研究动物园的现实。

sentences.en: But also there's, um, kind of an empirical answer, which is, do people who go to zoos, um, care less about animals because they're being objectified and, you know, restrained or do
sentences.zh: 但同时也有，嗯，某种经验层面的回答，那就是，去动物园的人，嗯，会因为动物被物化和，你知道的，被限制而减少对动物的关爱，还是

sentences.en: they care more about animals?
sentences.zh: 他们会更关心动物？

sentences.en: And I have consistently found that people in zoos seem to care more about animals.
sentences.zh: 而我一直发现，动物园里的人似乎更关心动物。

sentences.en: So, um, empirically the zoos seem to be having that positive effect.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，从经验上讲，动物园似乎确实起到了这种积极的作用。

sentences.en: And what else can people do to feel a greater connection to the environment?
sentences.zh: 人们还能做些什么来感受到与环境的更多联系？

sentences.en: Well, I think that we all, we are, um, not necessarily socially encouraged to feel that connection.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们所有人，我们，嗯，在社会上不一定被鼓励去感受这种联系。

sentences.en: Uh, so I think we need to be very deliberate about taking time out from our lives to, to feel connected.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以我认为我们需要非常刻意地从生活中抽出时间来，去感受这种连接。

sentences.en: I think for example, when I was, um, you know, picking a college or picking a graduate school, the idea that I would pick a particular place was almost, would be, was seen as
sentences.zh: 我想举个例子，当我，嗯，你知道的，在选择大学或研究生院时，那种我会选择某个特定地方的想法几乎是，会被，被视为

sentences.en: illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 不合理的。

sentences.en: You know, I should go on the basis of the program and the offerings and not on whether I like the campus.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我应该根据专业项目和课程来选择，而不是根据我是否喜欢这个校园。

sentences.en: Um, and I'm not saying people should pick a graduate school based on their campus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我并不是说人们应该根据校园来选择研究生院。

sentences.en: Um, but I do think that we, uh, we can be encouraged to pay a little bit more attention to the actual
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我确实认为我们，呃，我们可以被鼓励对我们身处的实际

sentences.en: place in which we find ourselves and, um, and then how to incorporate more nature into that place.
sentences.zh: 地方给予更多一点的关注，嗯，然后是如何将更多的自然融入那个地方。

sentences.en: So I'm fortunate that I'm on a campus that has lots of trees.
sentences.zh: 所以我很幸运，我在一个有很多树的校园里。

sentences.en: They have, uh, qualified as a tree campus and, um, really put a lot of effort into making it look attractive.
sentences.zh: 它们，呃，获得了树木校园的资格，嗯，真的花了很多精力让它看起来很有吸引力。

sentences.en: Uh, if you're at a place which doesn't have those advantages, maybe there are ways in which, uh, it could be tied to nature a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 呃，如果你身处一个没有这些优势的地方，也许有一些方法，呃，可以把它和自然更好地结合起来。

sentences.en: You know, if you have a, an outdoor space, maybe there could be more shrubs or more flowers because of course people really do benefit from those, those moments that they spend in
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你有一个户外空间，也许可以有更多的灌木或更多的花卉，因为当然人们确实从那些在

sentences.en: nature.
sentences.zh: 自然中度过的时光中受益匪浅。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Does it also help to bring nature inside the home, like by house plants or, you know, uh, you know, potted flowers, that kind of thing?
sentences.zh: 把自然带到室内也有帮助吗，比如通过室内植物，或者，你知道的，呃，你知道的，盆栽花卉之类的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think one of the questions that sort of is currently being investigated is how much nature do we need?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为目前正在研究的问题之一是我们到底需要多少自然？

sentences.en: You know, what's the dose response relationship here?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里的剂量反应关系是什么？

sentences.en: Um, we don't know the answer yet, but there's certainly, uh, research evidence suggesting that just having potted plants around, sometimes even posters of, of, of nature can be
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们还不知道答案，但肯定有，呃，研究证据表明，仅仅在周围摆放盆栽植物，有时甚至是自然的

sentences.en: helpful.
sentences.zh: 海报，都会有所帮助。

sentences.en: So yeah, do whatever you can.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，尽你所能去做吧。

sentences.en: And, um, the research does show that when you're in nature, you do feel more connected to nature.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，研究确实表明，当你身处自然之中时，你确实会觉得与自然的联系更紧密。

sentences.en: And, um, over time, hopefully that, that becomes a lasting or at least a semi-permanent, uh, sense of yourself.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，随着时间的推移，希望这能成为一种持久的，或者至少是半永久的，呃，对自我的感知。

sentences.en: And hopefully people become better stewards of the environment through, through that connection.
sentences.zh: 并且希望人们通过这种联系，成为更好的环境管理者。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: People who feel more connected to nature do tend to want to take care of it.
sentences.zh: 那些觉得与自然联系更紧密的人确实倾向于想要保护自然。

sentences.en: It, it, it feels more personal to them.
sentences.zh: 这，这，这让他们觉得更亲近。

sentences.en: Like they're not being asked to sacrifice for something they don't care about, but they're being asked to,
sentences.zh: 就像他们不是被要求为一个他们不在乎的事情做出牺牲，而是被要求，

sentences.en: they're being invited to have a more positive relationship with something that's important to them.
sentences.zh: 他们被邀请与对他们重要的事物建立更积极的关系。

sentences.en: And you also research environmental justice.
sentences.zh: 你还研究环境正义。

sentences.en: Can you talk about what that is?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那是什么吗？

sentences.en: Um, yes, there, I would say a couple of ways of thinking about environmental justice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我想说有几种思考环境正义的方式。

sentences.en: It's often used very specifically to refer to the idea that, um, we need to make sure that environmental costs and benefits are distributed fairly.
sentences.zh: 它通常被非常具体地用来指代这样一种观点，即，嗯，我们需要确保环境成本和效益得到公平分配。

sentences.en: So there's a long history of environmental injustice, um, in this country and around the world where numbers of minority groups, for example, um, tend to live closer to
sentences.zh: 因此，在这个国家和世界各地，环境不公有着悠久的历史，例如，许多少数族裔，嗯，往往离

sentences.en: toxic waste dumps, uh, and polluted areas.
sentences.zh: 有毒废物倾倒场和污染区域更近。

sentences.en: They tend to be farther removed from, you know, happy, healthy, natural environments, you know, parks and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们往往离那些快乐、健康、自然的坏境，比如公园等等，更远。

sentences.en: So we really need to be mindful of, uh, of the idea that that's one way in which injustice occurs is by, um, exposing people to these environmental harms and
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实需要牢记，呃，这种不公正发生的一种方式就是，嗯，让这些人暴露在这些环境危害中，而

sentences.en: not giving them equal access to the environmental benefits.
sentences.zh: 不让他们平等地获得环境效益。

sentences.en: Then I've also been interested in, uh, because justice has been one of my research interests, um, you know, throughout my career, um, I'm interested
sentences.zh: 然后我也一直对，呃，因为正义一直是我研究兴趣之一，嗯，在我整个职业生涯中，嗯，我感兴趣的是

sentences.en: in how people think about justice when it comes to environmental issues.
sentences.zh: 人们在面对环境问题时是如何思考正义的。

sentences.en: Do they tend to conceptualize it in particular ways as opposed to the way in which they might think about justice in the workplace, for example?
sentences.zh: 与他们思考职场正义的方式相比，他们倾向于以特定的方式对其进行概念化吗？

sentences.en: So how, how do they think about justice and how do their perceptions of justice influence the way they respond to environmental issues?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们是如何思考正义的，他们的正义感又是如何影响他们对环境问题的反应的？

sentences.en: And do you have any other research that you're working on right now?
sentences.zh: 你现在还有什么正在进行的研究吗？

sentences.en: Um, well, right now I'm, I'm focusing primarily on two things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，目前我，我主要专注于两件事。

sentences.en: One is, uh, I developed a scale a number of years ago, maybe, maybe 15 or, or maybe more, um, to measure what I call environmental
sentences.zh: 一个是，呃，我在多年前开发了一个量表，也许，也许15年，或者更多，嗯，来衡量我所说的环境

sentences.en: identity, which is that, that sort of lasting perception of oneself as being connected to an interdependent and the natural environment.
sentences.zh: 认同，也就是那种认为自己与自然环境相互依存并紧密相连的持久自我感知。

sentences.en: Um, and so that scale has been, has been widely used.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这个量表已经，已经被广泛使用了。

sentences.en: And right now I'm working with a number of people to see if we can validate it cross-culturally and
sentences.zh: 目前我正与许多人合作，看看我们是否能在不同文化和

sentences.en: with a number of different samples, because I did develop it primarily with college students.
sentences.zh: 许多不同的样本中对其进行验证，因为我最初确实主要是通过大学生来开发它的。

sentences.en: And then the other thing I'm working on is really trying to explore something we touched on earlier
sentences.zh: 然后我要做的另一件事是试图探讨我们之前提到的一点，

sentences.en: that, uh, distress and anxiety people feel when they think about climate change, even though they might not have directly experienced negative impacts.
sentences.zh: 即，呃，人们在想到气候变化时感受到的痛苦和焦虑，尽管他们可能没有直接经历过负面影响。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That'll be, I'm sure that'll be very fascinating what your findings are.
sentences.zh: 那将是，我确信你的发现会非常迷人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's definitely a big, there's a lot to explore there.
sentences.zh: 这里绝对有很多，有很多东西可以探索。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And in the students you teach, what are, what attitudes about the environment do you see, we see with the younger generation?
sentences.zh: 在你教的学生中，有什么，你看到了对环境有什么样的态度，我们在年轻一代身上看到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, of course there's a, I think there's a, perceived to be a, a socially correct response.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然有一个，我认为有一个，被认为是在社会上正确的回答。

sentences.en: So, um, they know that they're supposed to care about the environment.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，他们知道自己应该关心环境。

sentences.en: Um, but I think most of them actually do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为他们大多数人实际上确实如此。

sentences.en: And especially, uh, as I say, at my campus where we have this nice environment, people say sometimes they came here because they really liked the look of the campus.
sentences.zh: 特别是，呃，正如我所说，在我的校园里，我们有这么好的环境，有时人们说他们来这里是因为他们真的很喜欢这里的校园风貌。

sentences.en: Um, so very much people are concerned about the environment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以大家非常关心环境。

sentences.en: I do sense a fair amount of hopelessness.
sentences.zh: 我确实感觉到相当多的无望感。

sentences.en: Um, not quite what I would call despair, but just a pessimism.
sentences.zh: 嗯，倒不太算我所说的绝望，而只是一种悲观情绪。

sentences.en: Uh, so that, that's a general response.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以，那是一种普遍的反应。
